To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dietary phytochemical compounds are effective in animal models of cancer chemoprevention.
the redox status is the key regulator of the cell fate, and that the dietary cancer chemoprotective agents are the key modulators of the cell’s redox status.

dietary phytochemical electrophiles and reactive oxygen species are capable of modulating gene expression via redox-sensitive molecular signaling pathways, and that these redox-mediated differential gene expression responses are responsible for cytoprotection in normal cells versus cytotoxity in tumor cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the redox circuit and its modulation by dietary cancer chemopretive phytochemical compounds.

elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying the cytoprotective effects of dietary chemopreventives, which may be used to prevent or delay cancer and other diseases, and the cytotoxic effects of these same compounds in cancer cells, which may be utilized for the development of cancer chemotherapeutic agents.

the redox circuit of cellular signaling, which is critical for normal cellular homeostasis, and the pharmacologic and toxicologic consequences of dietary phyto-chemicals, as well as synthetic drugs, in modulating the redox circuit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

redox-sensitive signaling mechanisms are important in the cytoprotection and detoxification of dietary anti-cancer phytochemicals and that the redox-sensitive Nf2-Keap1 axis is a key target of these compounds.
the redox circuitries of normal cells are different from those of tumor cells, which can be exploited in the design of new therapeutic interventions.
the redox circuit is a critical component of the signaling mechanisms of dietary phytochemically-mediated chemoprotection of normal versus cytotoxicity of tumor cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

redox-mediated signaling mechanisms in cyto-protection of normal cells and cytotoxicity in cancer cells provide a novel paradigm in understanding the mechanisms of action of dietary cancer chemoprotective compounds, and that this may lead to novel therapeutic strategies in the prevention and treatment of human cancers and other human diseases.

the redox circuitries of Nrf2 and NF-κB are the key players in the regulation of gene expression and cellular redox homeostasis, which is the key to the pharmacotoxicogenomics of chemopreventative and chemotherapeutic dietary phytochemical interventions in cancer.
dietary chemopreventative phytochemicals are effective against chemical-induced, as wells as genetic-induced, animal carcinogenic models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dietary phytochemical electrophiles are effective in cancer prevention by inducing phase II detoxifying enzymes, but they also have the capacity to induce apoptosis and cell death in cancer cells.
redox signaling mechanisms play a critical role in the cytoprotection and detoxification in normal cells versus cytotoxity and cell death mechanisms in tumor cells.

the redox circuitries in cells are critical for sensing and transducing oxidative/electrophile stress and that these redox circuits may be exploited for therapeutic intervention in diseases, especially cancers.
